newsitem.title: UK: Buba's Koebnick-Germany may miss EMU debt goal.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Koebnick-Germany may miss EMU debt goal.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick said the forecast of Germany's six leading economic institutes that Germany might fail to meet the Maastricht debt and deficit criteria might be realistic.
"This is most probably a pessimistic view, still I fear it may be realistic," he told reporters in London.
Koebnick, who was speaking in English, noted that the discount, Lombard and repo rates were all very low. Technically there was scope for the repo rate to fall further.
"We don't see a necessity at the moment to change any of these rates. There would be no effect," he said.
Koebnick said the general level of German interest rates was "good for the time being".
Asked if the Bundesbank planned to stick to fixed repos, Koebnick said markets were a bit uncertain about the outlook for rates and added, "for the time being it is good to stick to a fixed repo".

Commenting on the convergence criteria laid down by the Maastricht Treaty, he said there was flexibility in interpreting them but he believed a deviation of more than 10 percent from the 3.0 percent deficit/GDP ratio would not be acceptable.
"3.3 percent is too much," he said.
Asked if this meant 3.2 percent was acceptable, Koebnick replied "maybe," providing all the other factors insuring sustainability of monetary union were in place.

He reiterated his view that postponement of EMU by one or two years would not be a catastrophe. "It would be a catastrophe if we stick to the timetable and enter into currency union with destabilising elements," he added.
